verdict.headline: S&P 500 hits record as oil crash seals 1-of-6 regime; AMD and SpaceX sell off on strength
verdict.label: SPX 7,737 (new ATH, +1.79%); WTI $76.14 (−5.2%, $79 breach cleared); regime 1-of-6; PLTR $158.81 (+26.4%); AMD AH −8% on data-center $6.7B; SPCX AH −7%; September hike 54%; 30Y 5.20% sole breach
verdict.rationale_short: Every regime condition the morning outlined as the bull case materialized: SPX set a new all-time record, oil cleared the $79 threshold, September hike fell to 54% on cooling JOLTS. The AH tape told a different story — AMD and SpaceX each sold off roughly 7-8% despite beating estimates, confirming the morning's warning that AI hardware infrastructure was fully priced at elevated pre-earnings entries. One breach remains: the 30Y at 5.20%, still 20bps above 5.00%. Closing it requires a data sequence, not more oil. Friday NFP is the first test.

watchlist_mentions.note: $158.81 (+26.4% on the session). Full-session carry of Monday's AH beat. At $158.81, approximately 98-100x forward sales. The 149% US commercial growth rate is the justification, but Q3 must show the same order of magnitude to hold the multiple. Monday's DoD-vs-commercial structural shift (commercial grew faster than government) is now the baseline; any Q3 commercial deceleration below 100% at this multiple compresses the stock materially.

trade_setups.thesis: AMD printed $11.5B revenue (+50%) and $6.7B data-center revenue (+107%) then sold off 8% after hours. The morning was precise: AMD had risen from $484 to $518 before reporting, compressing the margin such that even a strong $6.7B data-center result repriced as a sell-the-news event from the elevated entry. The setup now is a post-selloff stabilization test: does $477-480 (implied AH) hold after the premium fully unwinds, or does the regular session continue the retracement toward the pre-PLTR-read-through range of $440-450? The $484 Monday close is the anchor; two consecutive closes below it signal the PLTR premium has fully reverted.
trade_setups.entry: Levels that define the setup: $518 (August 4 close before AH); $484 (Monday close, pre-PLTR premium); $477 implied AH settlement; $440-450 pre-read-through range.
trade_setups.invalidation: A close back above $518 signals buyers absorbed the AH selloff; a close below $440 signals the full PLTR premium retraced.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y yield — path to 5.00% through data sequence
trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y at 5.20% is the sole remaining regime breach, 20bps above the 5.00% formal clearing threshold. Oil deflation has already contributed most of its rate-relief over three sessions (approximately −8bps total). Closing the remaining 20bps requires labor and inflation data, not more oil. The sequence: NFP Friday below 80K pushes September well below 50%, giving the 30Y a technical path toward 5.00%. CPI August 13 below 3.0% would extend it. September at 54% is already 16 points below the 70% trigger; the question is whether NFP and CPI extend that gap or reverse it.
trade_setups.entry: 5.00% is the formal clearing level. Progress measured in bps. NFP Friday and CPI August 13 are the two data points that determine the path.
trade_setups.invalidation: NFP above 130K restores September above 70%, sends 30Y back toward 5.28%, and re-triggers the formal breach.
trade_setups.horizon: 1-3 weeks; NFP August 7 and CPI August 13 are the key dates

trade_setups.thesis: SpaceX's first public earnings showed $7.81B revenue (+92% YoY) beating estimates by 12.7%, with AI segment growing 247% YoY to $2.56B. But capex of $18.37B (vs $13.22B estimated) represents a 2.35x capex-to-revenue ratio — capital is being deployed into AI infrastructure faster than revenue can absorb it. The stock is already −45%+ from its June ATH. The structural question the setup poses: does the AI segment revenue trajectory converge toward justifying the capex burn by Q3 (reporting November), or does each quarter of elevated capex without proportional revenue acceleration further compress the stock? December 2026 lock-up expiry adds supply overhang.
trade_setups.entry: Levels defining the setup: $225.64 June IPO high; current implied AH range (~$120-130 estimated); $100 as psychologically significant at ~57% below IPO high.
trade_setups.invalidation: Q3 AI segment revenue above $5B (vs $2.56B Q2) or Starlink reaching operating profitability would break the capex-concern narrative upward.
trade_setups.horizon: Q3 earnings (November 2026) is the next quantitative test

bear_case: AMD delivered $6.7B in data-center revenue (+107% YoY), a 7% beat on consensus, and a Q3 guide of $13B — and the stock sold off 8% after hours. SPCX beat revenue by 12.7% — and sold off 7%. The tape is not rewarding AI hardware beats; it is selling the news on infrastructure plays priced to perfection. The 30Y at 5.20% is 20bps from clearing, but oil deflation has front-loaded its contribution; NFP Friday at 91K consensus is not soft enough to close the gap in one print. An above-130K surprise restores September above 70% and sends 30Y back toward 5.28%, reversing much of the week's rate-relief trade in a single morning. PLTR at $158.81 (approximately 99x forward sales) requires 149% US commercial growth to sustain quarterly through Q3; any deceleration below 100% compresses the multiple without the DoD urgency floor that previously supported it. If SPX closes below 7,380, this read does not hold.
